hero.heading: Open source AI for life science research.

knowledgeGraph.title: Knowledge Graph
knowledgeGraph.description: Understands how scientific concepts relate to one another, connecting ideas across research instead of treating them in isolation.

semanticSearch.title: Semantic Search
semanticSearch.description: Finds relevant research based on meaning rather than exact wording, so you get useful results even when you phrase things differently.

dataSovereignty.title: Data Sovereignty
dataSovereignty.description: Keeps your data within your own environment at all times, so nothing sensitive ever has to leave your control to use it.

openSource.title: Open Source
openSource.description: Everything about how the platform works is open and inspectable, so you're never dependent on a closed system you can't verify.

complianceControls.title: Compliance Controls
complianceControls.description: Built to meet the standards required in regulated research settings, helping institutions adopt the platform without extra compliance work.

labIntegration.title: Lab Integration
labIntegration.description: Fits naturally into the tools and workflows you already use, so your team benefits without changing how it works.

connect.heading: Connect the way you work
connect.subtitle: Use Lematter from the command line, in your code, or through the Model Context Protocol.

whatIs.question: What is Lematter?
whatIs.answer: Lematter is an open source AI platform for life science research, built to give grounded, citation-backed answers instead of generic AI responses.

different.question: How is this different from other AI tools?
different.answer: Lematter is built specifically for research and lab use — every answer is grounded in real sources with citations you can verify.

openSource.question: Is Lematter open source?
openSource.answer: Yes. The platform is open source, so anyone can inspect how it works.

selfHost.question: Can I self-host Lematter?
selfHost.answer: Yes, self-hosting is supported so your data can stay within your own infrastructure.

who.question: Who is Lematter for?
who.answer: Researchers, labs, biotech teams, and institutions that need trustworthy AI support for their work.

free.question: Is Lematter free?
free.answer: The open source core is free to use.
